record.paper_title: Some open problems in mathematical relativity
record.original_question: Can one prove long-time existence, as the trace of the extrinsic curvature tends to plus or minus infinity, for the cosmological vacuum Einstein equations in constant-mean-curvature slicing gauge?

evidence.quote: Show long-time (trK-1-±oo) existence in the CMC slicing gauge for the cosmological spacetime vacuum equations (this is the compact Cauchy surface version of a previous question).

artifact.self_contained_problem: Consider the vacuum Einstein equations Ric(g) = 0 on a globally hyperbolic spacetime (M, g) of cosmological type, that is, one admitting a compact Cauchy surface. A constant-mean-curvature (CMC) slicing is a foliation of M by spacelike Cauchy hypersurfaces Σ_τ whose induced second fundamental form K has trace tr K equal to a constant τ on each leaf, with τ serving as a time function. Working in the CMC slicing gauge (so that the lapse and shift are chosen so the time function coincides with τ = tr K), and starting from smooth vacuum CMC Cauchy data on a compact 3-manifold Σ for which the future development admits a CMC slicing, prove that the maximal CMC development extends so that τ ranges over a half-line tending to +∞ in the expanding direction and to −∞ in the contracting direction (i.e., long-time existence as tr K → ±∞ in the CMC slicing gauge for the cosmological vacuum Einstein equations).
artifact.status_search_result: The question of long-time existence in CMC slicing for the cosmological vacuum Einstein equations remains a major open problem in mathematical relativity. Partial results exist for special symmetry classes (e.g., U(1)-symmetric, surface symmetric, T^2-symmetric spacetimes) and under curvature/geodesic completeness assumptions, but the general case is unresolved. Recent work (2023–2024) has actually focused on obstructions: Galloway, Ling, and collaborators constructed vacuum cosmological spacetimes lacking any CMC Cauchy surface, indicating the global CMC foliation problem is still very active.

status_evidence.title: Existence of CMC Cauchy surfaces and spacetime splitting
status_evidence.snippet: Most existence results for CMC slices in globally hyperbolic spacetimes with compact Cauchy surfaces ultimately rely on barrier methods; general long-time existence remains conditional.
status_evidence.claim: General long-time existence in CMC gauge is not established and relies on geometric assumptions.

status_evidence.title: Vacuum cosmological spacetimes without CMC Cauchy surfaces
status_evidence.snippet: Vacuum cosmological examples without CMC Cauchy surfaces have been constructed, showing the CMC foliation problem is subtle and active.
status_evidence.claim: There exist vacuum cosmological spacetimes without CMC Cauchy surfaces, so the CMC slicing problem is still being investigated.

status_evidence.title: Theorems on Existence and Global Dynamics for the Einstein Equations
status_evidence.snippet: Long-time existence in CMC gauge has been proved only under symmetry assumptions or special conditions, not in full generality.
status_evidence.claim: The general long-time CMC existence question remains open.
